Water Pesources
There will be no significant impact by this proposed facility upon existing water resources as no natural waterways, lakes or streams will be crossed.
The natural watershed areas and surface streams encountered have already been altered by the presence of existing I-94 to the west and the airport to the east. At present the drainage systems flow into two concrete open channel sections of the Milwaukee Metropolitan Sewerage Commission drainage systems located north of Layton Avenue and Edgerton Avenue.
Effect upon these drainage channels would be minimized by crossing them with adequate bridge or culvert designs and by the necessary precautions taken at the time of construction. Current roadway maintenance practices indicate no significant pollution problem.
The City of Milwaukee's Holler Park pond located at the southwest corner of South 6th Street and Edgerton Avenue is adjacent to one of the proposed corridors but will not be affected. According to the Department of Natural Resources this small pond was constructed as part of a 16.4 acre county park consisting of one half acre pond with a maximum depth of four feet. The major water source for the pond is the metropolitan system which provides water from Lake Michigan. The pond is generally turbid over a clay bottom. Stocking of panfish sustains a summer fishery for disabled children, the park's principal users. Other major users are aesthetic and for skating. Because it is small and fairly isolated from major water courses, it has little use by water fowl.
The proposed project will not affect any public water supply source, treatment facility or distribution system.
